correctness.rationale: The m-1 interior Fourier eigenspaces are two-dimensional; two-site shell evaluation has determinant proportional to sin(pi k h/m) and loses exactly one direction at k=j m/g for 1<=j<g. The spatial-visible space thus has dimension 2m-g+1. A Vandermonde with pairwise distinct spectral multipliers demixes all m+1 shell values after m+1 time steps. At m steps its one-dimensional kernel has no zero entry, so the endpoint and degenerate shell ratios force beta=alpha and alpha=(-1)^(h/g)alpha, producing an additional transient 1D defect iff h/g even. Counting coprime offsets gives stated parity census; below m dimension bound forbids full recovery. Independently built exact SymPy matrices for all 2<=m<=7, 1<=h<2m and checked both rank formulas. For C6,h=2 ranks 5 at t=3, 6 at t=4; this is a precise test case, not the proof.

The primary 2011 Parlangeli–Notarstefano cycle observability theorem (4.10) expresses a full-n gcd criterion, seemingly conflicting with the explicit C6,h=2 spectral calculation; we do not silently treat it as dominating coverage. The candidate exact two-horizon formula follows from direct Fourier analysis, and residual convention/older-theorem reconciliation remains a live priority risk. A 2026 graph dynamical-sampling preprint could be inspected only at bibliographic/abstract level.

Permanent loss g-1, and if g=1 the minimum full-recovery horizon is m for odd h and m+1 for even h.
